subject: science

entries: Electric field lines run from + to −: between the charged plates each line draws straight from the positive plate to the negative one, evenly spaced, and the probe dot rides one line down to show the push on a positive charge.
slots.label: Electric field lines run from + to −
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A bar magnet's field loops from N to S: the lines leave the north pole, sweep round above and below the magnet and enter the south pole, never crossing and never ending in empty space.
slots.label: A bar magnet's field loops from N to S
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Moving the magnet changes the flux: pushing the magnet towards the coil grows the flux threading it and a voltage appears, but holding the magnet still lets the needle fall back to zero, because only the change induces an emf.
slots.label: Moving the magnet changes the flux
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A generator spins the coil in the field: as the coil turns the flux through it rises and falls between max and zero, and the induced emf alternates with the change, kicking the meter left then right.
slots.label: A generator spins the coil in the field
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: motion, not position: while the magnet sits still inside the coil the needle holds flat, and only when the magnet moves again does the changing flux kick the meter - position never induces, change does.
slots.label: A common mistake: motion, not position
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The field around a charge, drawn as lines running from + to -: a positive charge placed in it is pushed along the lines, and E = F/q. Between charged plates the evenly spaced lines mean a uniform field.
slots.label: Electric field
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The field around a magnet or current, drawn as lines that loop from N to S outside a bar magnet and never cross: the line direction at a point gives the direction of B there, and closer lines mean a stronger field.
slots.label: Magnetic field
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The amount of magnetic field threading a coil, Φ = BA cos θ, measured in webers (Wb): it is greatest when the coil faces the field squarely and zero when the coil is edge-on to it.
slots.label: Magnetic flux
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The induced voltage around a coil when the flux through it changes, emf = -N ΔΦ/Δt: it exists only while the flux is changing, never from flux merely being present.
slots.label: Emf
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The induced emf equals the rate of change of flux linkage, emf = -N ΔΦ/Δt, with the minus sign (Lenz's law) saying the induced effect opposes the change that produces it.
slots.label: Faraday's law
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
